meta.title: 1962 Canadian BCP, The Litany

sources.ref: The Book of Common Prayer (1962, Canada), The Litany, printed pages 30 to 36
sources.note: Text extracted with pdftotext -layout; speaker attribution follows the printed minister/people alternation and the explicit Minister/People labels in the Supplication.

caveats: Section headings are app aids for navigation, not printed rubrics.
The Royal Family placeholder and the bracketed Ember Ordination petition are retained as printed.
Speaker attribution in the main Litany is inferred from the printed alternation of long petitions and short responses.

lines.text: Which may be sung or said before the Holy Communion; or after the Creed at Morning or Evening Prayer, instead of the remaining part of the Service; or as a separate service, with Hymns, a Psalm, a Lesson, the Creed, and a Sermon, at the discretion of the Minister.
The Litany should always be used at least once a month on a Sunday, and is commended for use on Wednesdays, Fridays, and Rogation Days.
The Invocations
O God the Father, Creator of heaven and earth: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O God the Father, Creator of heaven and earth: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O God the Son, Redeemer of the world: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O God the Son, Redeemer of the world: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O God the Holy Ghost, Sanctifier of the faithful: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O God the Holy Ghost, Sanctifier of the faithful: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O holy, blessed, and glorious Trinity, three Persons and one God: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O holy, blessed, and glorious Trinity, three Persons and one God: have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: The Deprecation
Remember not, Lord, our offences, nor the offences of our forefathers; spare us, good Lord, spare thy people, whom thou hast redeemed with thy most precious blood.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Spare us, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: From all evil and mischief; from sin, from the crafts and assaults of the devil; from thy wrath, and from everlasting condemnation,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: From all blindness of heart; from pride, vain-glory, and hypocrisy; from envy, hatred, and malice, and all uncharitableness,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: From all uncleanness in thought, word, and deed; and from all the deceits of the world, the flesh, and the devil,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: From lightning and tempest; from earthquake, fire, and flood; from plague, pestilence, and famine; from battle and murder, and from sudden death,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: From all sedition, conspiracy, and rebellion; from all false doctrine, heresy, and schism; from hardness of heart, and contempt of thy Word and Commandment,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: By the mystery of thy holy Incarnation; by thy holy Nativity; by thy Baptism, Fasting, and Temptation,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: By thine Agony and bloody Sweat; by thy Cross and Passion; by thy precious Death and Burial,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: By thy glorious Resurrection and Ascension; by thy sending of the Holy Spirit; by thy heavenly Intercession; and by thy Coming again in glory,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: In all times of tribulation; in all times of prosperity; in the hour of death, and in the day of judgement,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Good Lord, deliver us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: The Supplication
We sinners do beseech thee to hear us, O Lord God: and that it may please thee to rule and govern thy holy Church universal in the right way,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To keep and strengthen in the true worshipping of thee, in holiness of life, and in devotion to her people, thy servant ELIZABETH, our most gracious Queen and Governor,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To be her defender and keeper, giving her the victory over all her enemies,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bless and preserve [ . . . . ] and all the Royal Family,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Here shall be named, as determined by authority from time to time, the several members of the Royal Family.
We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To be used in the Ember weeks, and on the day of an Ordination.

To bless thy servants at this time to be admitted to the Order of Deacons or of Priests, and to pour thy grace upon them; that they may duly execute their office to the edifying of thy Church, and to the glory of thy holy Name,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To send forth labourers into thy harvest; to prosper their work by thy Holy Spirit; to make thy saving health known unto all nations; and to hasten thy kingdom,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bless the people of our Country and the Commonwealth, and to endue those set in authority with grace, wisdom, and understanding,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bless and guide the judges and Magistrates, giving them grace to execute justice, and to maintain truth,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bless and keep the Queen’s forces by sea, and land, and air, and to shield them in all dangers and adversities,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To give to all nations unity, peace, and concord, that they may serve thee without fear,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bless and protect all who serve mankind by their labour and learning,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To preserve all that travel, all women labouring of child, all sick persons and young children; and to show thy pity upon all prisoners and captives,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To defend, and provide for, all widows and orphans, and all who are desolate and oppressed,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bless and keep all thy people,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To give to all thy people increase of grace, to hear meekly thy Word, and to receive it with pure affection, and to bring forth the fruit of the Spirit,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To bring into the way of truth all who have erred and are deceived,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To strengthen such as do stand; to encourage the faint-hearted; to raise up those who fall; and finally to beat down Satan under our feet,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To succour, help, and comfort all that are in danger, necessity, and tribulation,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To have mercy upon all men,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To give and preserve to our use the kindly fruits of the earth, so that in due time we may enjoy them,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To forgive our enemies, persecutors, and slanderers, and to turn their hearts,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: To give us true repentance; to forgive us all our sins, negligences, and ignorances; and to endue us with the grace of thy Holy Spirit, to amend our lives according to thy holy Word,
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: We beseech thee, good Lord.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Son of God, we beseech thee to hear us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Son of God, we beseech thee to hear us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O Lamb of God, that takest away the sin of the world;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O Lamb of God, that takest away the sin of the world;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Grant us thy peace.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O Christ, hear us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O Christ, hear us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Lord, have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Christ, have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Lord, have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: The Lord’s Prayer

Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy Name, Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our trespasses, As we forgive them that trespass against us; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from evil. Amen.
lines.speaker: all

lines.text: Then shall follow the Collect of the day.
A Prayer of Saint Chrysostom

Almighty God, who hast given us grace at this time with one accord to make our common supplications unto thee; and dost promise that when two or three are gathered together in thy Name thou wilt grant their requests: Fulfil now, O Lord, the desires and petitions of thy servants, as may be most expedient for them; granting us in this world knowledge of thy truth, and in the world to come life everlasting. Amen.
lines.speaker: all

lines.text: 2 Corinthians 13. 14.
The Grace
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Ghost, be with us all evermore. Amen.
lines.speaker: all

lines.text: When the Litany is read immediately before the Holy Communion, the Minister may proceed, after the Lord’s Prayer of the Litany, to the Communion Service, which may begin with the Mutual Salutation and the Collect of the day.
A Supplication
Which may be used before the Prayer of Saint Chrysostom in the Litany, or at other Services, especially in the Penitential Seasons and in times of trouble.
O Lord, arise, help us, and deliver us for thy Name’s sake.
lines.speaker: all

lines.text: O God, we have heard with our ears, and our fathers have declared unto us, the noble works that thou didst in their days, and in the old time before them.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O Lord, arise, help us, and deliver us for thine honour.
lines.speaker: all

lines.text: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O Lord, arise, help us, and deliver us for thy Name’s sake.
lines.speaker: all

lines.text: From our enemies defend us, O Christ;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Graciously look upon our afflictions.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Pitifully behold the sorrows of our hearts;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Mercifully forgive the sins of thy people.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Favourably with mercy hear our prayers;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O Son of David, have mercy upon us.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Both now and ever vouchsafe to hear us, O Christ;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Graciously hear us, O Christ; graciously hear us, O Lord Christ.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: Then shall be said one or both of these prayers, with the versicles preceding:
O Lord, let thy mercy be shown upon us;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: As we do put our trust in thee.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: We humbly beseech thee, O Father, mercifully to look upon our infirmities; and, for the glory of thy Name, turn from us all those evils that we most justly have deserved; and grant that in all our troubles we may put our whole trust and confidence in thy mercy, and evermore serve thee in holiness and pureness of living, to thy honour and glory; through our only Mediator and Advocate, Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: O Lord, deal not with us according to our sins;
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Neither reward us according to our iniquities.
lines.speaker: people

lines.text: O God, merciful Father, that despisest not the sighing of a contrite heart, nor the desire of such as be sorrowful: Mercifully assist our prayers that we make before thee in all our troubles and adversities, whensoever they oppress us; and graciously hear us, that those evils, which the craft and subtilty of the devil or man worketh against us, be brought to nought; and by the providence of thy goodness they may be dispersed; that we thy servants, being hurt by no persecutions, may evermore give thanks unto thee in thy holy Church; through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.
lines.speaker: minister

lines.text: Other prayers from this Book may be added, concluding with the Prayer of Saint Chrysostom and the Grace.
